description:
Maths for ages 4–10. Reading from age 6.
Short daily missions with pictures, games and rewards.
Free, with no ads or in-app purchases.

Geni Kids gives your child practice matched to their age. The daily mission combines maths and, from age 6, reading – and children choose which to do first.

Maths that grows with your child
• Ages 4–5: Count pictures, find who’s first and last, more or fewer, finger numbers and shapes. Questions are read aloud and chapters are short (10 exercises).
• Age 6: Addition and subtraction, number bonds to 10, doubles, days of the week and seasons, and telling the time on the hour and half hour.
• Ages 7+: Number line, tens and ones, mental maths, money, mirror symmetry, coding with a robot, bar charts, and a topic path through crossing ten, time, measurement and logic.
• Up to age 10: Times tables as groups, fair sharing, story problems, fractions, division, area and perimeter, units and 3D shapes.

Money in your own currency
The shop game uses the coins and notes where you live – pounds, euros, dollars and more.

Three ways to practise reading
Children can listen to a text, read independently, or read aloud with speech recognition. Reading is optional at age 6 and part of the daily mission from age 7.

Rewards for showing up
Coins, XP, levels, badges, streaks and challenges give children goals to work towards. Playful haptics make every right answer feel great.

Made for families
• Multiple child profiles, each with their own progress.
• A weekly summary for parents: days, exercises, accuracy, strongest and hardest.
• “School is working on”: pick the topics your child should practise more.
• A PIN-protected parent area.
• Works offline, with iCloud progress sync.
• No ads, no in-app purchases, no tracking.

Available in English, Norwegian, Spanish and Portuguese.

whatsNew:
• Every exercise now fits on the screen, on iPad in landscape and portrait and on iPhone. No more answers hidden below the edge.
• On iPad in landscape, clock, money and coding exercises show the picture beside the answers.
• "Listen to me read" asks for the microphone the first time, and shows how to turn it on if it's off.
• "Which one does not belong?" now uses clear everyday groups like fruit, animals and vehicles.
• Smoother scrolling in the parent area.
